To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the acute subcutaneous isoprenaline toxicity in rats depends on body temperature and the animal’s thermoregulatory ability.
isoprenaline-induced cardiac failure and myocardial lesions depend on the body temperature of the animals and the extent of the lesions is independent of the body temperature of animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of isoprenalina on body temperature and the effect of body temperature on toxicity of isoprenalin in rats.
the effect of body temperature on the acute toxicity of isoprenalin in rats.
the effects of temperature on the toxicity of isoprenalin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acute subcutaneous toxic action of isoprenalines is influenced by the thermogenic and thermoregulatory responses of an animal to the drug.
isoprenaline is not a cardiac toxicant but a cardiotoxicant, and that the cardiotoxicity of the drug is not dependent on its effect on body core temperature.
the effect of isoprenalene on body temperature and heart rate depends on the thermoregulation and the body surface area of an animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acute toxicity of isoprenalin is influenced by the thermodynamic properties of the animal, while the cardiotoxicity of repeated small doses is not.
the body temperature is an important factor influencing the cardiotoxicity of catecholamines, especially in the cold.
the body temperature is a major determinant of the acute toxicity of isoprenalin, but it does not affect the chronic toxicity of the drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the body temperature of animals should be monitored during toxicity testing, especially if the drug is known to affect body temperature, and the results of the toxicity tests should be adjusted to take into consideration the effect of body temperature.
the acute effects of isoprenalines depend on body temperature, which is influenced by the thermogenic capacity of an animal and ambient temperature.
the acute toxicity of isoprenaline is temperature dependent.
